ask: Which of the following describes what a queen excluder does?

options.t: Lets bees leave a box but not return
options.why: That is a bee escape board, which clears bees out of a box before harvest.

options.t: Lets workers pass but stops the queen
options.why: Its gaps fit a worker bee but not the larger queen.

options.t: Narrows the entrance against robber bees
options.why: That is an entrance reducer at the front of the hive, not a grid between boxes.

options.t: Holds a new queen while bees accept her
options.why: That is a queen cage, used when a colony gets a new queen.

explain: A queen excluder has gaps that fit a worker but not the bigger queen, so only workers reach the boxes above.

ask: Which of the following parts sits between the brood box and the honey boxes for the whole season?

options.t: Bee escape board
options.why: A bee escape board sits there only for a day or two before harvest, not all season.

options.t: A cloth laid over the top frames
options.why: A cloth over the frames sits on top of the highest box, not between brood and honey boxes.

options.t: Queen excluder
options.why: It stays between the brood box and the honey boxes all season so no brood ends up with the honey.

options.t: A block that narrows the entrance
options.why: That block sits at the front opening at the bottom of the hive.

explain: The excluder goes on when the honey boxes do and stays until they come off.

stem: A beekeeper lifts the honey boxes in midsummer and finds eggs and young brood in the frames that were meant for honey only. The queen has been laying up there.
ask: What should the beekeeper fit between the brood box and the honey boxes?

options.t: A cage holding a new queen
options.why: A cage holds a queen while a colony accepts her. It does not keep her out of the honey boxes.

options.t: A queen excluder
options.why: It lets workers through but keeps the queen below, so she can no longer lay in the honey boxes.

options.t: A block narrowing the entrance
options.why: Narrowing the front opening does nothing about where the queen lays.

options.t: A bee escape board
options.why: A bee escape board clears all bees out for a harvest. It is not meant to stay on and keep the queen down.

detail: eggs and young brood in the frames that were meant for honey only
explain: Eggs in the honey boxes mean the queen walked up there. A queen excluder lets workers through but stops her.

stem: At a club workshop, a new member asks why the grid between two of the boxes has gaps of one exact width. The leader says the width is the whole point of the part.
ask: Which of the following explains the exact gap width?

options.t: Workers pass and the queen cannot
options.why: The width is chosen so a worker fits through and the larger queen does not.

options.t: It lets bees out but not back in
options.why: That one-way exit belongs to a bee escape board, not to a grid with even gaps.

options.t: It keeps mice out in winter
options.why: A mouse guard does that at the entrance. The grid's gaps are sized for bees.

options.t: It lets the hive breathe in summer
options.why: Air flow comes from the entrance and vents. The gap width is about the queen.

explain: The grid is a queen excluder: the gap width is what sorts the workers from the queen.

stem: A hobby beekeeper is setting up a hive for the season and wants the top boxes to hold only honey, with no brood mixed in.
ask: Which of the following describe how a queen excluder helps with this? (Select TWO)

options.t: Its gaps let workers pass but stop the queen
options.why: With the queen kept below, no eggs are laid in the top boxes.

options.t: It lets bees leave a box but not return
options.why: That is a bee escape board. It would empty the top boxes of workers too.

options.t: It stays in place for the whole season
options.why: It is on as long as the honey boxes are, so the queen never gets up there.

options.t: It is removed a day before harvest
options.why: That timing fits a bee escape board. An excluder stays on all season.

options.t: It narrows the entrance against robbers
options.why: That is an entrance reducer. It does not decide where brood ends up.

explain: The excluder keeps the queen below, so she lays no eggs in the honey boxes, and it stays on all season.

stem: A beekeeper reads the inspection notes below for one hive.
ask: Which of the following MOST likely explains the brood in the top box?

lines: Hive 4, 12 June: top box frames 3 to 6 hold capped brood
Hive 4, 12 June: grid between boxes found bent, one corner lifted
Hive 4, 12 June: brood box frames normal, eggs present

options.t: A missing bee escape board
options.why: A bee escape board is only used before harvest. Its absence would not let the queen up.

options.t: An open entrance reducer
options.why: The entrance is at the bottom of the hive. It has nothing to do with the top box.

options.t: A cracked inner cover
options.why: The inner cover sits above the top box. A crack there does not open a way up from the brood.

options.t: A bent queen excluder
options.why: The notes say the grid between the boxes is bent with a corner lifted, which leaves a gap the queen can use.

detail: grid between boxes found bent, one corner lifted
explain: A bent grid leaves a gap the queen can squeeze through, and the brood in the top box shows she did.

ask: Which of the following describes what a bee escape board does?

options.t: Narrows the entrance against robber bees
options.why: That is an entrance reducer at the front of the hive.

options.t: Keeps the queen in the lower boxes
options.why: That is a queen excluder, which sorts bees by size.

options.t: Feeds sugar syrup from inside the hive
options.why: That is a frame feeder. An escape board holds no food.

options.t: Lets bees leave a box but not return
options.why: Its one-way exit lets bees walk down and out of the boxes above it, with no way back.

explain: A bee escape board has a one-way exit, so the boxes above it empty of bees.

ask: Which of the following parts is placed under the honey boxes only a day or two before harvest?

options.t: Queen excluder
options.why: A queen excluder stays on all season, not just before harvest.

options.t: Bee escape board
options.why: It goes in a day or two before harvest to clear the honey boxes of bees.

options.t: A block that narrows the entrance
options.why: That block sits at the front opening, not under the honey boxes.

options.t: A cloth laid over the top frames
options.why: A cloth over the frames goes on top of the highest box.

explain: Only the escape board is timed to the harvest: it clears the honey boxes and then comes off.

stem: On harvest morning, a beekeeper wants to lift off the full honey boxes without carrying thousands of bees to the kitchen. She has one evening left to prepare.
ask: What should the beekeeper place under the honey boxes that evening?

options.t: A queen excluder
options.why: An excluder only stops the queen. The workers would still fill the boxes.

options.t: A cage holding a new queen
options.why: A cage holds one queen. It does nothing about the thousands of workers.

options.t: A bee escape board
options.why: Overnight the bees walk down through its one-way exit, so the boxes are nearly empty by morning.

options.t: A block narrowing the entrance
options.why: Narrowing the front opening does not clear the honey boxes.

explain: A night under a bee escape board is enough for the bees to leave the honey boxes and not come back.

stem: A beekeeper slides a board under the honey boxes one evening. By morning most bees have gone down into the brood box, and very few come back up.
ask: Which of the following explains why the bees stay below?

options.t: Its gaps are too narrow for the queen
options.why: Gaps sized for the queen describe a queen excluder, and workers pass an excluder freely.

options.t: Smoke drove them down
options.why: No smoke was used here. The board did the work overnight.

options.t: Its exits open only one way
options.why: The one-way exits let bees go down but give them no way back up.

options.t: The top frames ran out of food
options.why: The honey boxes are full of food. The bees left because they could not return.

explain: The board is a bee escape board: its exits work one way, so bees that go down cannot return.

stem: A beekeeper will harvest tomorrow and plans to clear the honey boxes of bees overnight, without sprays or brushing.
ask: Which of the following are true of the part that does this? (Select TWO)

options.t: It stays on the hive all season
options.why: That is a queen excluder. The part here is only used for a night or two.

options.t: Bees can leave through it but not return
options.why: That one-way exit is how it clears the boxes overnight.

options.t: It stops only the queen from passing
options.why: That describes a queen excluder, which would leave the workers in the boxes.

options.t: It goes under the honey boxes
options.why: Placed under the honey boxes, it lets the bees above walk down and out.

options.t: It is sprayed with a scent bees avoid
options.why: That is a fume board, and the stem rules out sprays.

explain: A bee escape board goes under the honey boxes and lets bees out one way, with no spray and no brush.

stem: A club member posts the messages below after a harvest.
ask: Which of the following would have been the BEST part to fit the night before?

lines: Club chat, 08:10: Took the honey boxes off hive 2 this morning.
Club chat, 08:11: Half the colony came with them into the kitchen.
Club chat, 08:12: I had put a grid between the boxes last night.

options.t: A fume board
options.why: A fume board also drives bees out of honey boxes, but it works in minutes on the day, not set the night before.

options.t: A queen excluder
options.why: The grid was most likely an excluder, and it left the workers in the boxes.

options.t: A bee escape board
options.why: Set the night before, its one-way exit would have emptied the boxes of bees by morning.

options.t: An inner cover
options.why: An inner cover sits on top of the hive and clears no bees.

detail: Half the colony came with them into the kitchen
edge: Both clear bees from honey boxes. A part fitted the night before points to the bee escape board, which works over hours.
explain: The bees came along because nothing had cleared them. A bee escape board set the night before would have.

source.chapter: Choosing what goes between the boxes
